transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Huang (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CobaltHealth CTO), Devon Park (CobaltHealth ML Eng), Priya Nair (CobaltHealth SRE)

Auto summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Quick sync to review last week's POC instability spikes (timeouts, 5xxs), confirm immediate mitigations (client-side retries + exponential backoff), and plan longer-term tuning (batching, KV cache warmups, route fallback). Agreement to run controlled 24h load with backoff and share trace.

Topics:
- Recent 5xx patterns and root-cause hypotheses
- Retry/backoff strategy and client-side limits
- Rate limiting: token buckets and per-customer concurrency caps
- Observability gaps: missing request ids and tracing hops
- Next steps: load run, runbook, sample trace export

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, quick roll call and then we'll jump in. Marta?
[00:07] Marta: Hi, Marta here. Sorry bit of background noise on my end.
[00:09] Devon: Devon here.
[00:11] Priya: Priya, SRE.
[00:13] Samir: Great. Lena, you good to run the triage notes?
[00:16] Lena: Yeah, I'll try. So we looked at the last three spikes, um, mostly 5xxs clustered around 11:30 and 14:45 UTC yesterday, right around your peak batch jobs.
[00:27] Devon: Yeah that matches what we saw. There were some timeouts too, client-side timeouts after about 8 seconds, then we retried three times which made the load even worse.
[00:36] Marta: Quick note, our client retry logic is currently immediate, no backoff. It's a library default.
[00:40] Samir: Ok that explains amplification. We recommend exponential backoff plus jitter, and cap retry attempts to two for user-facing calls.
[00:49] Priya: Question: is Redwood doing any server-side quick throttling that could cause 429s? We saw 5xx not 429 though.
[00:57] Lena: Good question. The runtime will sometimes return 429 if a token-bucket is exceeded, but in these traces most responses were 502/503 returned by the inference engine when upstream GPU pool ran out of memory or OOM-killed a worker, or the model process crashed.
[01:12] Devon: We did see a bunch of 502s that line up with a sharp increase in long context requests — some requests had 8k tokens which we didn't expect.
[01:21] Samir: Ah, long context. Were those from a single route or many different calls?
[01:26] Devon: Mostly from a single workflow path in our ingestion pipeline — a batch QA step that got misconfigured to send full logs.
[01:33] Marta: That was our mistake, we reverted that job but the retries from the client kept hitting you guys.
[01:39] Lena: Right. Two quick mitigations we discussed: client-side backoff + short-term rate-limit on the route, and server-side cap on max tokens per request.
[01:48] Priya: How aggressive should the rate-limit be? We're worried about breaking users in the POC.
[01:53] Samir: Start soft: 5 RPS per user with a bursting window of 20 for short spikes, then iterate. We'll monitor error rates.
[02:02] Devon: If we cap tokens per request server-side, can Redwood provide a clear error so our client can trim inputs?
[02:08] Lena: Yes we can return a structured error with code MODEL_TOO_LONG and include the token count and your quota in the body — though note in some transcript logs that field might get cut off, transcription aside.
[02:20] Marta: Perfect.
[02:22] Samir: On retries, set max attempts to 2 with exponential backoff starting at 200ms, doubling with jitter. Do not retry on 4xx or MODEL_TOO_LONG.
[02:34] Priya: For the 5xx pattern, do you have any root cause? OOM, kernel panic?
[02:40] Lena: From the debug logs: a mix. Some workers crashed during KV cache warmup because the sequence length exploded memory usage; others were preempted by the hypervisor when our GPU pool ran high, producing 502s.
[02:52] Devon: Hypervisor preemption — are those dedicated GPUs or shared?
[02:56] Samir: In this POC you're on a small shared pool — so preemption is possible during noisy neighbor events. For Dedicated we can guarantee pinned capacity.
[03:07] Marta: Hmm, budget constraints push us to shared for now. Any mitigations short of dedicated?
[03:12] Lena: Yes: warm up KV caches during low-traffic windows, limit context length, and use smaller batch sizes for those heavy routes. Also configure retry/backoff to avoid amplification.
[03:22] Samir: We also suggested statically quantized model variant for internal batch jobs — reduces memory by ~30% in our tests.
[03:29] Devon: Ok that could help. Please share the quantization tradeoffs doc, specifically latency delta and quality drift.
[03:36] Samir: Will do. I'll attach the Benchmark + QC notes in the follow-up.
[03:40] Priya: Observability gap — we lack consistent request ids through our pipeline, so it's hard to trace a single user path.
[03:47] Lena: We noticed that too. Suggestion: add a client-generated request_id header and propagate through Redwood, we'll ensure it shows up in our logs and tracing spans.
[03:56] Devon: We'll add that.
[03:57] Marta: Also saw some mismatched timestamps between our logs and Redwood logs, small timezone offsets, might be causing confusion.
[04:03] Lena: We log UTC always; maybe your agents were local time.
[04:06] Marta: Yeah I think our ingestion worker emits local time.
[04:09] Samir: Ok noted.
[04:12] Lena: Next, we started a controlled 4-hour load yesterday but it didn't use exponential backoff because the client didn't implement it; results showed memory climbs then OOM in a subset of pods.
[04:24] Devon: Do you have flame graphs or heap dumps we can look at?
[04:28] Lena: We captured a heap snapshot from one crashed pod — attaching to the follow-up. It's noisy but shows large KV cache allocations when sequence length jumps.
[04:37] Priya: Any quick config changes we can do today?
[04:39] Samir: Short-term: 1) enable client exponential backoff, 2) add a server-side max_tokens=2048 for the route, 3) temporarily lower concurrency to 10 for the route during peak.
[04:52] Marta: We'll do that after this call.
[04:54] Devon: One more question about rate-limits: do you support per-route and per-api-key caps?
[04:59] Lena: Yes both. We also have per-model caps. In the hosted tier we can apply per-api-key buckets; in dedicated you can customize further.
[05:08] Priya: For our SLOs, we need P95 latency below 300ms for small prompts. Do you think the throttling will push us over?
[05:16] Samir: Throttling can increase client-perceived latency if your client waits and retries; but with proper backoff and lower retry counts, P95 should be fine. We'll monitor.
[05:24] Devon: Are there any silent retries on Redwood's side we should be aware of?
[05:28] Lena: No silent retries in the path — retries are client-driven. We do have internal short-circuit fallbacks between model variants when a slow model is detected, but those are explicit and logged.
[05:39] Marta: Can we get the fallback config? We worried about surprise model switches.
[05:44] Samir: Yes, we'll share the rollout policy doc; by default we don't switch models without a canary period.
[05:50] Priya: Security check — for prod we will need KMS integration. For the POC, is data retained on Redwood?
[05:57] Lena: Hosted retains logs for 7 days by default; we can shorten retention or turn on redact-on-ingest for PII. For Private you'll control retention. We'll send the SOC two and ISO sheet too.
[06:10] Marta: Good.
[06:12] Samir: Quick recap: immediate owner tasks — Lena runs a 24h load with exponential backoff and smaller batch sizes, Devon provides scrubbed traffic trace, Samir sends runbook + security links.
[06:24] Devon: Timeline for 24h run?
[06:27] Lena: Start tomorrow and share results by Friday.
[06:30] Marta: We'll also push a config change to cap tokens per request.
[06:33] Samir: Great. Any other blockers?
[06:36] Priya: None from SRE side.
[06:38] Marta: Nope.
[06:40] Samir: Alright thanks everyone, I'll follow up with notes and the docs.
[06:45] Devon: Thanks.
[06:47] Meeting end.
